topLine: The ICAC's Operation Rosny hearings dominated NSW politics, with the inquiry hearing that developer Toplace paid $134,000 for a private investigator to surveil a former Strathfield mayor, and that the former Labor councillor who arranged it allegedly joked about the surveillance. In policy, the Minns government announced an extra 1,000 prison beds and moved to tighten ticketless parking fine rules, while a $1.2bn Sydney datacentre proposal was withdrawn with the developer blaming shifting state and federal regulation. Locally, Shoalhaven Council adopted a 30-year community infrastructure blueprint and is weighing visitor parking fees to fund road repairs.

briefing.localWatch: Shoalhaven ratepayers face two live council decisions: a newly adopted 30-year infrastructure blueprint and a proposal to charge visitors for parking to help pay for local roads. Works on the historic Nowra Bridge and the mayor's return to duty after cancer treatment round out the local picture.

stories.headline: Council adopts 30-year blueprint for community infrastructure
stories.summary: Shoalhaven City Council says it has adopted a 30-year plan for community infrastructure, according to a council notice.

stories.headline: Pay to park? Shoalhaven considers visitor parking fees to help fix local roads
stories.summary: The South Coast Register reports Shoalhaven City Council is considering charging visitors for parking as a way of raising money for local road repairs.

stories.headline: The 'Harbour Bridge treatment' as historic Nowra Bridge given major facelift
stories.summary: The South Coast Register reports the historic Nowra Bridge is undergoing major refurbishment works.

stories.headline: 'Just let me die': Shoalhaven mayor back at work after harrowing cancer battle
stories.summary: The South Coast Register reports the Shoalhaven mayor has returned to work following a battle with cancer.

stories.headline: Right to Know Week: Upholding Information Integrity in the Digital Age
stories.summary: Kiama Council has published a notice marking Right to Know Week, which it frames around public access to information and information integrity.

stories.headline: Narooma payphone heritage-listed for connecting people when mobiles failed during black summer bushfires
stories.summary: Guardian Australia reports a public payphone in Narooma on the NSW south coast has been heritage-listed, recognising its role during the 2019-20 black summer bushfires when mobile networks were knocked out and residents and tourists queued to contact family and friends.

stories.headline: Meet the Keira independent who gives herself a shot to take down Ryan Park
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury profiles an independent candidate contesting the Illawarra seat of Keira, held by Labor's Ryan Park, who the paper reports believes she has a chance of unseating him.

stories.headline: Extra 1,000 prison beds announced in NSW as union warns against arresting ‘our way out of domestic violence’
stories.summary: Guardian Australia reports the NSW government has announced an extra 1,000 prison beds, with a union cautioning against trying to arrest "our way out of domestic violence". The Sydney Morning Herald reports on a prison that sat abandoned for years and is now set to reopen as domestic violence offenders add pressure to the corrections system.

stories.headline: Plan for controversial $1.2bn datacentre in Sydney scrapped due to ‘emerging’ regulations
stories.summary: Guardian Australia reports plans for a $1.2bn datacentre at Lane Cove, known as "Project Mars", were withdrawn from the NSW planning portal on Monday. Developer Goodman Group attributed the decision to the policy and regulatory environment for large-scale datacentres, citing "emerging" state and federal rules.

stories.headline: Minns Labor Government to tighten ticketless parking fine rules amid 87% drop in 2025-26
stories.summary: The NSW government says it will tighten the rules governing ticketless parking fines, pointing to an 87 per cent fall in such fines in 2025-26.

stories.headline: ‘False hope’: MP slams 10-dam flood plan
stories.summary: The Daily Telegraph reports an MP has criticised a 10-dam flood mitigation plan, describing it as "false hope".

stories.headline: Back to work: prison guards ordered to end snap strike after courts halt
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports prison officers have been ordered back to work after a snap strike that brought court operations to a halt.

stories.headline: $12.4 million for North Coast active communities
stories.summary: The NSW government has announced $12.4 million for active community projects on the North Coast.

stories.headline: New shark surveillance drone tech rolling out as coverage is boosted for school holidays
stories.summary: The NSW government says new drone technology is being rolled out for shark surveillance, with coverage increased over the school holidays.

stories.headline: Developer paid $134k bill to spy on Sydney mayor, corruption inquiry told
stories.summary: The ICAC has heard that developer Toplace paid a private investigator $134,000 to surveil a former Strathfield mayor, Matthew Blackmore, with the operation described to the inquiry as a "personal matter" for company lawyer and Labor councillor Sharangan Maheswaran. Mr Maheswaran, who is under investigation over allegations of blackmail and illegal surveillance, told the inquiry on Tuesday that he hired the investigator, and the commission heard he allegedly made jokes about spy equipment and the song Every Breath You Take. No findings have been made.

stories.headline: Wine, snacks: Taxpayers in the red for minister’s minibar booze bill
stories.summary: The Daily Telegraph reports taxpayers covered a minister's minibar expenses, including alcohol and snacks.

stories.headline: Labor's Tiana Myers steps down during first term of council
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports Labor councillor Tiana Myers has resigned during her first term on council.

elsewhere.text: With Victoria's state election two months away, a DemosAU poll shows Labor improving but the Coalition still ahead on two-party preferred, The Conversation reports.
